form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Paul introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance

form.official-title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to permit withdrawals from certain retirement plans for repayment of student loan debt, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Higher Education Loan Payment and Enhanced Retirement Act of 2019 or the HELPER Act of 2019.

subsection.text: Paragraph (14) of section 401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:

subparagraph.header: Distributions for qualified higher education expenses

clause.text: A distribution shall be treated as made upon hardship of the employee to the extent that the aggregate amount of such distributions during the taxable year does not exceed the lesser of—

subclause.text: the amount paid by the taxpayer for qualified higher education expenses during such taxable year, or

clause.text: Clause (i) shall not apply to any distribution which is permissible under paragraph (2)(B)(i) (including distributions which would be treated as made upon hardship of the employee without regard to this subparagraph).

Clause (i) shall apply without regard to any requirement to demonstrate financial need or hardship, or to demonstrate that other assets are not available to pay the qualified higher education expenses.

clause.header: Additional tax under section 72(t) not to apply
clause.text: No tax shall be imposed under section 72(t) on any amount treated as a hardship distribution by reason of clause (i).
For purposes of this subparagraph, the term qualified higher education expenses has the meaning given such term by section 72(t)(7).

subsection.text: Paragraph (11) of section 403(b) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following: Under rules similar to the rules of section 401(k)(14)(C), a distribution shall be treated as made upon hardship of the employee to the extent that the aggregate amount of such distributions during the taxable year does not exceed the lesser of the amount paid by the taxpayer for qualified higher education expenses during such taxable year, or $5,250..

Paragraph (1) of section 457(d) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following: Under rules similar to the rules of section 401(k)(14)(C) (and without regard to whether the expenses are unforeseen), a distribution shall be treated as made by reason of unforeseen emergency to the extent that the aggregate amount of such distributions during the taxable year does not exceed the lesser of the amount paid by the taxpayer for qualified higher education expenses during such taxable year, or $5,250..
The amendment made by this section shall apply to distributions made after December 31, 2019.

section.header: Penalty-free withdrawals from IRAs for student loan expenses

subsection.text: Paragraph (7) of section 72(t) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:

subparagraph.text: Such term shall include amounts paid in repayment of any loan made to an individual described in subparagraph (A) to assist the individual in attending an educational organization described in section 170(b)(1)(A)(ii).

subsection.text: The amendment made by this section shall apply to distributions made after December 31, 2019.

section.header: Exclusion of distributions for educational expenses

subsection.text: Section 402 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:

subsection.header: Distributions for qualified higher education expenses

paragraph.text: Gross income for the taxable year does not include—

subparagraph.text: any distribution from a qualified cash or deferred arrangement (as defined in section 401(k)(2)), an annuity contract described in section 403(b), or an eligible deferred compensation plan described in section 457(b) which is maintained by an eligible employer described in section 457(e)(1)(A), which is treated as made upon hardship of the employee by reason of section 401(k)(14)(C), the last sentence of section 403(b)(11), or the last sentence of section 457(d)(1), or
any distribution from an individual retirement account (as defined in section 408(a)) to which section 72(t)(2)(E) applies.
An amount shall be treated as described in paragraph (1) only to the extent that such amount would be includible in gross income without regard to such paragraph.

In determining whether a distribution would be includible in gross income but for this subsection, rules similar to the rules of subsection (l)(3)(B) shall apply (by taking into account all retirement plans in which the taxpayer is a participant).

paragraph.header: Coordination with American Opportunity and Lifetime Learning credits

subparagraph.text: Paragraph (2) of section 25A(g) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by redesignating subparagraph (C) as subparagraph (D), by striking and at the end of subparagraph (B), and by inserting after subparagraph (B) the following new subparagraph:

a distribution from a qualified cash or deferred arrangement (as defined in section 401(k)(2)), an annuity contract described in section 403(b), an eligible deferred compensation plan described in section 457(b) which is maintained by an eligible employer described in section 457(e)(1)(A), or an individual retirement account (as defined in section 408(a)) which is excluded from gross income of the distributee under section 402(m) (other than any portion of such a distribution which is attributable to the repayment of a loan described in section 72(t)(7)(C)), and
Subparagraph (B) of section 72(t)(7) is amended by inserting (without regard to subparagraph (C) thereof) before the period.

paragraph.header: Deduction for interest on education loans
paragraph.text: Paragraph (1) of section 221(e) of such Code is amended by inserting before the period at the end the following: , or for any amount paid with a distribution which is excluded from gross income under section 402(m).

subsection.text: The amendment made by this section shall apply to distributions made after December 31, 2019.

section.header: Inclusion of employer student loan payments in educational assistance programs

subparagraph.text: the payment, by an employer, of amounts in repayment of any loan made to the employee to assist the employee in attending an educational organization described in section 170(b)(1)(A)(ii),

subsection.text: Paragraph (1) of section 221(e) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended by section 4, is further amended by inserting which is excluded from gross income under section 127 or is after or for any amount.
The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2019.

section.header: Repeal of cap on deduction for interest on education loans

subsection.text: Section 221 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking subsections (b) and (f).
Section 221 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as so amended, is amended by inserting after subsection (a) the following new subsection:

If the amount of the deduction allowable under subsection (a) exceeds the taxable income of the taxpayer for the taxable year (determined without regard to this section), then an amount equal to such excess shall be treated as interest paid by the taxpayer in the succeeding taxable year on a qualified education loan.
The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after the date of the enactment of this Act.
Subsection (a) of section 402A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended—

paragraph.text: by striking and at the end of paragraph (1);
by redesignating paragraph (2) as paragraph (3); and
by inserting after paragraph (1) the following new paragraph:

in the case of a qualified cash or deferred arrangement (as defined in section 401(k)(2)), any designated Roth employer contribution made pursuant to the arrangement shall be treated for purposes of this chapter in the same manner as contributions described in section 401(k)(3)(D)(ii), except that such contribution shall not be excludable from gross income, and
Paragraph (1) of section 402A(b) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended—

subparagraph.text: by striking may elect to make and inserting “may elect—
to make
by striking the period at the end and inserting , and; and
by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:

in the case of a qualified cash or deferred arrangement (as defined in section 401(k)(2)), to have the employee's employer make designated Roth employer contributions in lieu of all or a portion of the matching or nonelective contributions the employee is otherwise eligible to receive under the arrangement.

paragraph.text: Paragraph (2)(A) of section 402A(b) of such Code is amended by striking of each employee and inserting and designated Roth employer contributions with respect to each employee.

Subparagraph (B) of section 402A(d)(2) of such Code is amended by inserting , or elected to have made a designated Roth employer contribution, after designated Roth contribution both places it appears in clauses (i) and (ii).

subsection.text: Subsection (c) of section 402A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended—

paragraph.text: by inserting and designated Roth employer contributions after designated Roth contributions in the heading; and
by adding at the end the following new paragraph:

subparagraph.text: The term designated Roth employer contribution means any contribution described in subparagraph (B) made under a qualified cash or deferred arrangement (as defined in section 401(k)(2)) which—

clause.text: is excludable from gross income of an employee without regard to this section, and
the employee designates (at such time and in such manner as the Secretary may prescribe) as not being so excludable.

subparagraph.text: The contributions described in this subparagraph are—

clause.text: matching contributions (as defined in section 401(m)(4)(A)) which meet the requirements of subparagraphs (B) and (C) of section 401(k)(2), and
qualified nonelective contributions (within the meaning of section 401(m)(4)(C)).

subparagraph.text: The amount of matching contributions and qualified nonelective contributions which an employee may designate under subparagraph (A) shall not exceed the excess (if any) of—

clause.text: the maximum amount of such contributions excludable from gross income of the employee for the taxable year (without regard to this section), over
the aggregate amount of such contributions with respect to the employee for the taxable year which the employee does not designate under subparagraph (A).

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall apply to contributions made in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2019.

subsection.text: Subsection (k) of section 401 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraph:

subparagraph.text: A cash or deferred arrangement shall not be treated as failing to meet any requirement of this subsection solely because, under the arrangement, an employee may elect to make additional elective deferrals which are not subject to, and are not taken into account under, paragraph (3) to a separate account from other contributions made on behalf of the employee under the arrangement, if—

clause.text: all employees eligible to participate in the arrangement are eligible to make such election,
the aggregate of all elective deferrals made by the employee under the arrangement does not exceed the limitation of section 402(g), and
no matching or nonelective contributions may be made to such account or with respect to elective deferrals contributed to such account.

subparagraph.text: The rules of this subsection, other than paragraph (3), shall apply to any account established under subparagraph (A).

For purposes of this paragraph, the term elective deferral means any employer contribution under a qualified cash or deferred arrangement to the extent not includible in gross income for the taxable year under section 402(e)(3) (determined without regard to section 402(g)).

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall apply to contributions made in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2019.
